invariant: 2^64+1 matches §4's normative number grammar, so it is a NUMBER token and not a string — the precondition this case rests on. A decoder MUST therefore either represent it exactly or apply a DOCUMENTED out-of-range policy (§4, restated in the §13.2 checklist). The value sits above every implementation's ceiling except python's, making it the rust/python fault line the pairwise matrix cannot reach from an encoder
refs: SPEC.md v4.1 §4 number grammar (normative): an unquoted token decodes as a number iff it matches /^-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:e[+-]?[0-9]+)?$/i — so this token is a number, not a string

SPEC.md v4.1 §4: implementations MAY return a higher-precision type, a string, an approximate value, or reject the token IF that is the documented policy; implementations MUST document their out-of-range policy, lossless-first RECOMMENDED
SPEC.md v4.1 §13.2 decoder checklist: document the numeric out-of-range policy (§4)
